That is the pre-R12 projected A, with the old s7 structure, authored 54.1 s timing and the earlier events. diagnosis.retained_selection_reasoning: No supported route lets the retained selection bind the current film. (1) Technical continuation: the last two conditions are skipped only when caption_renderer_continuation(...) is truthy. Per the HOLD note, which I can't check because I did not read that function, it is limited to line-count-preserving caption, layout or legibility renderer edits. The R13 renderer diff I read adds lines (the moved flag, the s7 slide, the s8 id map) and changes behaviour structurally. More decisively, continuation never suppresses the concept condition 'current opening is not the selected concept', which has no continuation escape. (2) Metadata baseline: metadata_continuation.baseline only substitutes a geographic-metadata baseline board. R13 changed scene structure and timing, not geographic metadata, and no baseline can make da75de80 equal the current concept. (3) Inspection adoption: inspect_retained/adoption_problems only re-inspect the unchanged retained capture under a known orchestrator. They preserve the original selection, which still names concept da75de80. legacy_capture_problems also requires renderer_digest(board) == receipt renderer_sha256, which now fails. Adoption cannot clear the concept or renderer conditions. (4) Relabelling the selection, or carrying it to the changed concept, would rebind a provider verdict made on other films (a.mp4 f9ee6f15, b.mp4 bf004224) to bytes it never saw. That would be a false selection, and the instructions forbid it.
diagnosis.film_defects_in_current_bytes: None known. In report 24 I passed the current A bytes (5a1b8e26) at code-plan scope with no blocking defect. Captions (a6b0e45a, 16 measured cues, all inside 59.4 s), claims (49b2379c, which I re-read in full this round: the figure is c4 'initial assessments post-training', the chip and TinyML are c3 and c18, and the board's attribution matches), the script (67d7ae45) and the soundcheck at the 59.4 s cut (CHOSEN, take1, acc 0.992) carry no defect I can see. Nothing in this refusal is a film defect. It is an evidence-binding requirement. Pixels and audio remain unjudged, as before.
diagnosis.avoidable: Not avoidable in substance. The F3 runtime correction (splitting s7 at a measured clause boundary so the measured read fits the 9.5 s ceiling) necessarily changes A's scene structure and concept, and the renderer had to learn the s8 ids. So a new two-treatment comparison of current previews was always going to be mandatory once the take 7 measured read replaced the projected timing. The comparison policy binds the produced film to an independent selection between actual previews of the current concepts and renderer. What was avoidable is the spent charge. The 14-gate picture precheck does not include creative_production.opening_problems, and preflight_animatic runs that check only after capture_guard authorize --prepare has charged the hook (preflight_renders 19 to 20). A binding check before authorization would have caught it. 02-picture.md says daily_production.py --board --claims 'requires the bound comparison before narration'. I can't confirm that command reports opening_problems or that it is charge-free, so treat this as a process recommendation, not a finding.

renewal_plan.precondition_findings: The renewal can't use 'the restamped B (opening-b.json)' as it stands, and storyboard.json is not byte-equal to opening-a.json. I verified both against opening_compare.build. (1) Line 278 requires creative.read(root/'storyboard.json') in boards. The live storyboard.json (5a1b8e26) differs from opening-a.json (12c90919) in narration_picture.timing_provenance.word_content_sha256, by my own diff in report 24, so build raises 'opening alternatives must belong to the current owned edition and provisional board'. (2) Line 280 requires body(boards[0]) == body(boards[1]). Under treatment_required, body includes runtime_s, credits_s, native_media, the viewer question and each scene's id, start_s, duration_s, vo and vo_claims. A has runtime 59.4 with measured scenes s1 8.68 to s9 3.90, where s7's vo is two sentences and s8's vo is 'The announcement reports no field result. It names no town...' with claims c1, c4, c10. B has runtime 54.1 with projected scenes s1 7.76 and so on, s7 with three sentences and s8 with one sentence and claims c1, c10. build raises 'two alternatives must share dated facts, narration, timing and assets'. (3) Line 282 requires equal s1 durations, 8.68 against 7.76, so it raises again. (4) Line 326: an existing openings/comparison.json with a different reservation identity raises 'preserve the rejected comparison in the defect package before a changed batch'. The retained package must therefore be preserved elsewhere and the live path vacated before the batch. The batch then writes openings/a.json, b.json, a.mp4 and b.mp4 over the retained files, which would break the retained_files hashes in finish-current-capture-plan-r13b.json, because file_problems re-reads those paths.

classification.basis: The refusal is a mechanical binding consequence of the already-reviewed technical correction F1/F3 (runtime): the measured take 7 read forced runtime 59.4 and the measured s7/s8 split. That changed A's concept and renderer, and the comparison binding follows from it automatically. The conformance work it now requires for B is the same runtime correction applied to the second treatment: retime B to the measured read and split s7 at the same measured clause boundary. I am not force-fitting legibility, layout, source, rights or technical_audio: none of them applies, and nothing here is a creative or picture defect.
